## What

Everyone gets a working toolchain and proves it on real hardware before any
project work starts.

- **Everyone:** Vivado/Vitis (the version the Kria board files support), plus
  PetaLinux *or* Kria Ubuntu on the KV260. Pick one Linux and write down which.
- **Hardware members:** KiCad, and build a toy CPU connector board in it.
- **Repo:** this repository, the issue tracker and the shared notes. Mostly in
  place already; finish what is missing (setup steps, a place for meeting notes).

## Done when

- [ ] Every member has loaded a blinky onto the KV260. Record the Vivado version
      that worked in `docs/SETUP.md`.
- [ ] Every hardware member has finished the toy KiCad project.
- [ ] `docs/SETUP.md` takes a new member from nothing to a blinky without them
      having to ask anyone.

## Notes

The Vivado download is large and the licence step trips people up. Do it in the
first meeting, together, rather than as homework.
